title: HOKUM
review: Movie was an absolute banger. Adam Scott killed this one. I went into the movie knowing nothing about it except that one super creepy poster and what I got was something completely different, something that wasn't so much a horror movie as it was a character movie. The writing around Bauman (Scott) is so phenomenal that the scariness and unsettling feelings the picture brings gets washed away every time the screen is not dark. When it's dark though it feels claustrophobic - set design really plays a huge part in the tension you feel when watching. I think some of the witch stuff could have been a bit scarier; it's just an ugly old woman. The actual idea of the hotel having a lot unknown  monsters behind its walls is more scary then the witch. I think at some parts I was like ok what is happening but everything kind of pointed towards the main character and his backstory in a great way, to the point where I could ignore the sudden switches in movie style. When I say that I mean some parts looked like cheap horror and the other parts really meshed together well, the parts where we see other characters. All in all great film

title: Michael
review:
Mmmmmm honestly not the best movie but not boring at all. I think the biggest flaw of this movie was that the lead actor wasn't Michael Jackson. I didn't come from that era of music but all I know about the king of pop is that he made girls faint left and right and would move like he was a spring, almost alien/machine like. 

I mean the actor did a great job. I feel like I see his face now when I think of Michael Jackson, but that might be because I didn't really grow up listening to MJ.

The highlight of the movie was definitely Michael as a kid singing his heart out in the studio. That kid really killed it, he sounded just like Michael in the recordings. His movement and expressions really seemed authentic.

The movie had me looking up Michael's lore after. I didn't know that he had burned his head or had exotic pets - I wish they got into some of the weirder stuff that happened later in his career. I really enjoyed the acting of Joseph Jackson - he really did a good job portraying a cold father who simultaneously loves his family and is blinded by greed.

I think the coolest part about this movie is that someone from my high school was playing Tito Jackson. He actually had a couple of good lines in the movie too. Ryan Hill - good job ur making Torrance proud.

title: Obsession
review:
10/10. Actors definitely played a huge part in the success of this movie because the premise has been done many times; Monkey's Paw etc etc. 

I think the best part of the movie is how realistic the friend group was before everything went horribly wrong. The only parts of the movie where I didn't feel extreme anxiety was when either Sarah or Ian was in the shot ( besides that scene ). Every other scene post snap was so anxiety inducing because Inde does an extremely good job of portraying Nikki as an absolute psychopath that flutters between normal and monster in a snap, so its like your always waiting for classic horror stuff to come but most of the time its like a mix of Nikki being normal but some twisted stuff is happening so you can never really tell what is going on inside her head. 

Bear is absolutely awesomely terrible in this movie. Such a good example of a selfish wimp who has charisma but just doesn't know how to portray it to the person that really matters to him because he's unable to face the possibility of rejection like a pussy. When I say he has charisma it's because we see him with Sarah and Ian, like he isn't like super socially awkward, just completely selfish af.

This movie rocks, and will be a defining horror movie for our generation

title: Exit 8
review:
This is the movie you should watch instead of Backrooms. Just kidding, I haven't seen Backrooms (yet) so I can't judge, but wow its hard to top this one. Exit 8 is about a guy with asthma trying to exit a subway station and he finds out that he can't escape, stumbling upon the same exact corridor even as he keeps moving forward. The only way he can advance (he starts at exit 1 and the end is exit 8) is by finding something off about the current corridor. So he walks and walks, checking off every little detail of the white tiled subway corridor until he finds something wrong, at which point he is to turn around and "advance" through the never ending station. 

This movie is phenomenal in the way it advances the story while staying in the exact same place. Every time he "resets" and comes back to the first level in despair, you are anxious to see what is the next glitch in the station he will find. With each glitch you get more and more details about some of the strange things he sees and the tension is real.

Awesome movie

title: Tuner
review:
I have mixed feelings about this one. 

On one hand, the premise is cool - a piano tuner with extremely sensitive ear, to the point that the sounds of the world hurt him, that uses his curse to break into safes with just his hearing. He also meets this girl and the romance is real between them.

On the other hand, that's as far as the stakes go. His biggest enemy is an air horn, seriously. That sounds like a joke but I'm not even joking that's his biggest opp. 

The redeeming factor about this movie is the piano scenes and the romance. Both gave me chills during the intense scenes - a feeling I realized I haven't felt in a really long time.

The main character is a bit unlikeable and he runs weird but all in all I think worth a watch.

title: Backrooms
review: Walked out. I was at the part where they go down into the nasty room through the small dark slide. I didn't like it because the premise is just right there in the name. The main actor is good but yea it's just weird stuff in weird places.

title: Toy Story 5
review: After Toy Story 3, Toy Story 5 is my favorite of the series. The playing scenes really stuck out to me; it communicates the feeling of imaginative playing so well and brings an importance to the mission of the toys to bring happiness to their human companions. The palette during those scenes really added to the warmth and joy it brings.

title: The Furious
review: I do not understand how this movie has a 98% on rotten tomatoes. Really makes me question the credibility of that site. The movie is literally one big fight. Don't get me wrong, the choreo is amazing but honestly I would like it if we could go 5 seconds without Karate.

title: Scarface
review:
Although this movie is a staple "gangster film" and hailed as a masterpiece, I had never watched it until this last Sunday. 

I'm glad I did. Although the runtime is a bit long, it didn't feel long at all. Every scene in the movie held its own and the performance by Al Pacino is despicably amazing. The mark of a true masterpiece is that by watching it, you can understand why other movies or shows were made in the way they were - the influence is crazy (Vince Gilligan!!). Tony Montana is truly about that life - and at no point in the movie did I question his values or actions; they all aligned with clashing values of self-sufficieny as well as his overwhelming pride.

This movie is a non-stop adventure of someone who literally doesn't care about anything except himself. Even the scene with Hector Salamanca, which is arguably the only scene where he protects rather than destroys - I feel he made the choice he did because he woudln't be able to live with himself, rather than looking out for others.

Brian De Palma sets my new standard for what a true gangster is; someone who isn't cool or slick, rather someone who is so far gone to truly believe that the world is solely for him.

title: The Odyssey
reviewTitle: Absolutely breathtaking but also has some flaws
review:
I didn't see this movie in 70mm IMAX. One of the few theatres that has a realMax screen is in San Francisco ( AMC Metreon ), but I was too excited about this movie coming out that I just saw it in standard AMC laser.

Odysseus is truly him in this movie. Nolan does an amazing job of portraying the weight of Odysseus' name. My favorite scenes in the movie are the story of the Trojan Horse told by Menelaus, the scene with the dog for his homecoming, and the Laestrygonians. Honestly, it would be hard to mess this up; its like Nolan has so much content to work with its actually amazing he managed to tell a story that feels complete. 

Here are some of my criticisms of the movie.

1. The script/casting/acting - For some scenes of the movie, I felt like tone and delivery of the lines were very robotic; and the conversation between characters didn't flow naturally. I remember noticing this distinctly at some points. Also, maybe my listening comprehension is bad but I couldn't understand some of the lines at the beginning of the movie. I think someone who did an amazing job and deserves MVP is Menelaus. Also Robert Pattinson is awesome. Tom Holland, go back to playing spider guy.

2. Some parts could have been done better.
I swear the biggest climax of the movie took like an hour to happen. Odysseus is finally home and is about to see his wife that has been holding it down for 10 years, but from the moment hes like in the same room as her to the moment that she realizes its him, there is a long battle scene with some minion suitors that just didn't need to happen. I wish Odysseus would have just ran into Penelope's arms and there was like a grand kiss scene and everything woudl have been awesome; but the buildup just didn't pay off. I also wish we got to hear more about some of the adventures, like the sirens and the giants and the dead; some parts just felt a bit rushed and I wish they played with some more complex themes instead of battle battle battle ocean ocean row death.

Even though I have these things I hold against the movie, I think it was one of the most enjoyable films to watch in my life. I mean, the legend of the story of Odysseus combined with the triumphant and flawless pictures of Nolan is like the most perfect juicy combo ever. I'm probably going to watch it again in 70mm once the hype dies down.

title: The Invite
review:
Solid. The dialogue in this movie is phenomenal. Edward Norton was a standout, his calm and almost overly level-headed demeanor really sold his true acceptance of his crazy habits.

I am not the biggest Seth Rogen fan - just because he is one of those actors that plays the same character in every movie. His trademark panting and laugh didn't take away from the movie though; I think he was an excellent cast for the partner of Olivia Wilde's character, who is actually psychotic.

The fact that 99% of the movie was filmed in one house is crazy; I would think that it would feel claustrophobic but honestly the dialogue was so interesting and the pacing was so excellent that I didn't even notice and I didn't feel any stagnancy.

title: Minions And Monsters
review: Walked out, this movie is for toddlers.

title: Supergirl
review:
The movie had its moments. I wish we learned more about the little girl's family and their backstory on being legendary weaponsmiths.

I liked Kara's angst, but she didn't go ham enough. I think the movie did a good job for the purpose of setting up the DC universe, but still I left feeling a bit underwhelmed.

title: Disclosure Day
reviewTitle: Honestly, way better than I expected
review:
I went into this movie thinking it was going to be a stupid aliens come to Earth cliche movie but honestly it was actually really good. Every moment pushed onwards and the mystery aspect of this film really hit the spot for me. 

Some things were weird, like you never really know what the little device is and you never really understand the aliens outside of oooh they're aliens but I think spielberg did a great job of conveying a message about humanity through a story about aliens.

title: Spiderman: Brand New Day
review: Pack your bags, Tom Holland. This movie cemented your place as the worst spiderman.

title: The Prestige
review:
Right before I watched this movie I looked up its reviews online and my eye caught a phrase (I.T.) that absolutely spoiled the movie for me. I didn't know exactly what the phrase meant because that was literally all I knew about the movie, but after the bird scene with Olivia's nephew, I knew exactly where this was going. But honestly, that small spoiler made my watch of this movie much more interesting.

The Prestige is a movie that gets better the second time you watch it. I had the rare experience of having my first watch be like the second. I was able to appreciate the small details and the foreshadowing; yet the movie still surprised me in the end even though I had been expecting the reveal for the entire movie.

Since I just watched The Odyssey a couple weeks ago, I would say that this movie is on par or even slightly better than The Odyssey in its storytelling aspect, but Odyssey definitely beats this movie in terms of the visuals as well as its premise. So I'll give them the same rating :)
